summary.text: A 3-year-old girl was admitted with recurrent rashes for 3 months and limb weakness for 2 months. Examination showed red maculopapules, Gottron's papules and cutaneous ulcers, grade IV muscle strength and normal tone. Laboratory tests showed raised ESR, ferritin, D dimer and myogenic enzymes, and the myositis spectrum was positive for anti-MDA5 and anti-RO-52 antibodies. EMG, MRI of the femoral muscles and chest CT were abnormal.

She was diagnosed with anti-MDA5-positive JDM complicated by ILD and received IVIG, glucocorticoid, hydroxychloroquine, tacrolimus and tofacitinib with trimethoprim-sulfadiazine prophylaxis. Myogenic enzymes and ferritin decreased and CT showed some improvement. Twenty days later her dyspnea progressed with oxygen saturation of 92%–93%, infectious serologies were negative, and CT and laboratory indicators worsened.

Given her diagnosis of RP-ILD, she was treated with intravenous cyclophosphamide followed by three plasma exchange sessions, which gave symptomatic relief and improved laboratory indicators, but lung CT showed no significant change. Intravenous tocilizumab was then started at 10 mg/kg, was well tolerated, and was followed by marked CT improvement. She continued oral glucocorticoid, hydroxychloroquine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, pirfenidone, IVIG, cyclophosphamide and regular tocilizumab.

Follow-up CT confirmed substantial improvement, with absorption of lung inflammation and consolidation. After 6 months of follow-up her condition was stable and the glucocorticoid dose was gradually reduced to 5 mg/day. The authors report six cycles of tocilizumab over 4 months.
